newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms rating on Manufacturers Life Mtg bonds.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms rating on Manufacturers Life Mtg bonds.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it had affirmed its AA plus rating on Manufacturers Life Mortgage Securities Corp's $148.5 million 8.25 percent commercial mortgage-backed bonds series 1987-1 due March 1, 1997.
S&P said it had withdrawn its rating on a related series of securities, the 7.75 percent bonds due March 1, 1993, which were paid off.

"The affirmation is based on the obligation of Manufacturers Life Insurance Co (Manufacturers Life; AA plus claims-paying ability rating) to preserve the value of the mortgage collateral and to provide a return on nonmortgage assets sufficient to make annual simple interest payments on the bonds and to retire the bonds at maturity," S&P said in a statement.

"On the collateral side, Manufacturers Life is obligated to advance scheduled principal and interest payments on pledged mortgage loans that are delinquent and to contribute additional loans to the issuer in an amount sufficient to cover any deficiencies realised upon the liquidation of defaulted mortgage loans," S&P said.

"As of June 1996, the assets of the issuer totaled about $162.5 million. This comprised $1.7 million in mortgage assets, $0.2 million in the collection account, and $160.6 million in the prepayment account."
S&P said at the same time, the liabilities of the issuer totalled about $152 million, including accrued interest on the bonds.
"S&P expects that there will be no need for Manufacturers Life to contribute additional capital in order to retire the outstanding bonds in March 1997," the agency said.
S&P said based on its assessment of the credit quality of the pledged mortgages, it regarded the limited capital funding agreement as adequate credit support.
"To date, Manufacturers Life has made no unreimbursed advances, leaving the full $30 million available to cover any potential losses on the remaining $1.7 million in outstanding mortgages," S&P said.
